payload.mechanism:
The reader's snapshot-key derivation is PROSE INTERPRETED BY THE AGENT, not code — and it exists in two live copies whose text disagrees. That, not "a non-deterministic reader", is the root cause of the cycle-snapshot cache miss.

COPY A — .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md:58 (the declared SSOT):
    TICK = current UTC time formatted as HH:MM (round to nearest 5-min slot, e.g. 02:05 -> "02:05")
COPY B — .claude/skills/step-0-cowork/SKILL.md:39:
    TICK = current UTC time as HH:MM (e.g. "02:05")

Copy B has NO rounding clause — it specifies the RAW wall clock. Copy B's own header says "Full protocol: .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md" and then restates the rule inline instead of deferring to it, which is how the two drifted apart. Its example value "02:05" is itself on a 5-min boundary, so the copy reads as if it rounds without ever saying so.

alert-commander reaches BOTH: docs/agents/alert-commander/init.md and docs/agents/alert-commander/flow/stage-bootstrap.md both reference step-0-cowork, while cycle-bootstrap is named as the full protocol. 12+ agent files across market-watcher, digest-predict, bctc-analyst, qa-responder reference step-0-cowork too.
payload.token_blindness:
NEITHER copy mentions scheduled_utc — measured, 0 occurrences in both files. A spec-compliant reader is therefore token-blind BY SPECIFICATION, not by bug.

This partially REINSTATES my original claim, which I withdrew too broadly at cf302f00e. Precise position now: token-blindness is real and specced (established at the source); what the c253 sample correctly falsified was only the stronger claim that observed behaviour is UNIFORMLY token-blind — c253 probed the nominal 07:45, which neither copy authorises, so at least one invocation used the token on its own initiative. Both halves stated so this is not re-litigated a third time.
payload.evidence_ledger:
Six consecutive alert-commander cycles, probed key read from the committed notebook prose in every case (c250-c252 recovered from git history — c252 was pruned from the live file by c255's AC-2 retention, so the live notebook no longer holds it):

c250 07:08:22Z tick=07:05 -> probed 07:05  HIT   consistent with Copy A (rounded)
c251 07:24:44Z tick=07:22 -> probed 07:22  miss  consistent with Copy B (raw)
c252 07:37:30Z tick=07:30 -> probed 07:35  miss  consistent with Copy A (rounded)
c253 07:52:16Z tick=07:45 -> probed 07:45  miss  NEITHER copy authorises this - nominal/token
c254 08:08:49Z tick=08:05 -> probed 08:05  HIT   consistent with Copy A (rounded)
c255 08:11:39Z tick=08:05 -> probed 08:05  HIT   consistent with Copy A (rounded)

Distribution: Copy-A-consistent x4, Copy-B-consistent x1, unexplained x1. 3 hits of 6.

INFERENCE, not proof: the notebook never records WHICH copy a cycle followed, so copy-A-vs-copy-B is the explanation that fits, not an observed fact. What IS observed is that the two copies differ textually and both are reachable.

c254 and c255 are the controlled pair - same agent, same flow, spawned in the same second by the 08:00Z tick, both probed 08:05. They AGREE. So the derivation is not per-invocation noise within a tick; it varies across ticks. This retires my registered prediction (2) with a negative result.
payload.fix_design_impact:
Requirements this adds to the fix already routed at cf302f00e:

1. BOTH copies must change in the same commit. Changing only the declared SSOT leaves Copy B live and the drift continues. Preferred shape: delete Copy B's inline restatement entirely and leave only its existing "Full protocol ->" pointer, so there is one rule, not two.
2. The reader rule must become a token read, not a clock read: derive the key from the scheduled_utc prompt token's HH:MM portion. This is why the scheduled_utc Consumer Contract (spawn-fanout.md, currently scoped to "the leading 10 characters" = the date, for publish-marker keys) must be EXTENDED before it can be wired here - extend-then-wire, not wire.
3. Writer side unchanged from cf302f00e: tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7 keys the filename AND the in-file .tick off raw `date -u +%H:%M`; both go to the nominal tick.
4. Delete the stale note at cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md - "The snapshot writer (cowork-team dispatcher) is a future task. Until it lands, Step -1 will always miss and fall through to Step 0 - zero behavior regression." CONFIRMED still present at the SSOT. The writer has been live all day; this note tells every reader the miss is expected.
5. Newly measured, unrelated to the key: the freshness window is 7 minutes (both copies, step 2). The writer lands at roughly tick+5..8min and readers probe at roughly tick+7, so same-tick readers are inside it - but the margin is thin and neither copy anchors the window on the nominal tick either.

Why writer-and-reader must land together, restated correctly: a writer-only change TRADES the coincidental hits for deterministic ones and nets positive only once the reader is pinned. All 3 hits above were coincidental - the writer's raw clock happened to land on the same 5-min slot the reader's rounding produced.
